core.text: Preserve twelve correct sealed releases by boundary 13, source and inspection order, whole-load unloading, five rack places, two trolley allowances, and uninterrupted active operations. Rank transfer occupied minutes only among complete successes; transfer output is nine carriers and inspection output twelve.

Attack the account that powered trolley service is necessary for timely release. Hypothesis from the finite model: consecutive hand trips starting at 0 deliver B4 through B12 at boundaries 1 through 9 and permit continuous inspection through 13. The surviving function is timely rack supply, achievable without power; this route occupies nine transfer minutes. Closest rival: trolley loads B4-B7 during 0-3 and B8-B11 during 3-6, then hand B12 during 6-7, predicts completion at 13 with seven transfer minutes.

Preserve the failure signature: a ten-bracket mark accompanies an observed count of nine. Proposed conditional action selects WHERE: with that counted signature on the active carrier, act at inspection through correction, recount and sealing; with an empty eligible queue and a next source carrier instead, act at transfer by starting a permitted hand trip when its clerk is free. Do not classify every missing release as trolley failure. A fresh builder must show a consequential action conditional on the classified signature, beyond simply restating mandatory correction.

Probe the same boundary trace: record source unload identities, rack eligibility, active inspection count and duration, completed correct releases, and both clerks occupied intervals. Supply-starvation predicts an empty eligible queue and inspection idle time; B9 correction predicts an occupied counting surface with nine brackets and a two-minute inspection. Defeat the sensor claim if these observations do not separate the accounts or conditional control cannot outperform its closest feasible rival.

residue.text: Removing power can preserve output while increasing transfer burden. Waiting also occupies that clerk; the separate inspector cannot assist transfer. Eleven normal inspections plus B9 correction consume all thirteen inspection minutes, so any inspection idle time defeats the deadline. No additional capacity or staff can rescue it.

The anomaly cause remains unknown and implies no other defects. Later smaller requests are an unobserved hypothesis. Proposed schedules and sensor benefits are model predictions, not trial results or global optimality proof; the known discrepancy alone does not establish a new transport opening.
